key_insight: LLMs can generate correct finite element code, but consistency across attempts and independent verification remain critical barriers to trust.
engineering_relevance: Automating nonlinear mechanics and structural dynamics coding requires numerical validation beyond passing an agent’s own tests.
method: Extend FEM-Bench to 17 finite element tasks and evaluate 15 models on implementation and test generation.
Compare single-pass generation with two execution-and-revision harnesses for six models.
Analyze 249 failed agentic trajectories and explore separate coder and tester agents.
evidence_signal: The exploratory coder–tester configuration achieved 97.6% probability of at least one success across three attempts and 88.8% probability that all three succeeded.
watch_item: Self-tests can falsely reassure: 28.5% of failed agentic trajectories had tests sharing an error with the implementation, and the separate-agent results remain exploratory.
paper_title: Scientific Coding with Large Language Models: Evidence from Finite Element Analysis
